clue.text: Design that sounds like a set of rustic steps

indicators.note: the setter says the wanted word is pronounced the same as the thing described next

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a country fence

explanation.surface: A garden designer admires a rustic set of steps in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Style is the particular manner or fashion in which something is made, so it is a synonym for a design.

clue.text: Terrible bores at university become serious

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
a student in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Students who drone on dreadfully at university eventually grow serious.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means being in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: To sober up is to stop being frivolous or drunk and turn grave, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Cathedral is to dismiss clergyman when one's gone

indicators.note: one is the figure I, and its going means that letter is dropped from the clergyman

parts.note: in cricket, to york a batsman is to bowl him out with a yorker
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A cathedral chapter debates sacking one of its clergy once a colleague has left.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket verb 'york', to dismiss with a ball pitched at the batsman's feet, is the obscure piece; minister loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: York Minster is the great Gothic cathedral of the city of York in northern England.

clue.text: Former statute, correct in every detail

parts.note: ex- is the prefix for former
an act of Parliament is a statute

explanation.surface: An old law is described as being precise in all its particulars.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise and accurate, so it is a synonym for correct in every detail.

clue.text: Golden Hind, empty, sank unexpectedly in a Baltic port

indicators.note: emptying a name removes its insides, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: the two outside letters of the ship's name

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out in a surprising way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Drake's ship the Golden Hind, emptied of crew, goes down off a Baltic harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Golden Hind was Sir Francis Drake's ship; here only its outer letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a major Polish seaport on the Baltic Sea, formerly called Danzig.

clue.text: Book band

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the opening book of the Bible
second meaning: the English rock group of Peter Gabriel and Phil Collins

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two meanings: a biblical book and a famous progressive rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is the first book of the Old Testament and also the name of a well-known British rock band.

clue.text: Capone leaving one country for another

definitions.note: stands for 'another country', the noun supplied by the wordplay

indicators.note: the gangster departing means his short name is taken out of the larger word

parts.note: a country, the source word
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: The gangster Capone emigrates from one nation to a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver must think of the country Australia, which the clue only implies; removing Al from it leaves a different country.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a separate nation in central Europe, so it is the other country the clue asks for.

clue.text: Tennis star carrying new type of fastener

indicators.note: the star's name carries the other letters inside it as a load

parts.note: Marat Safin, Russian former world number one

indicators.note: making the word new means remaking it with its letters in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tennis player is seen wearing a novel sort of clip.
explanation.walkthrough: Marat Safin won the US Open in 2000 and the Australian Open in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety pin is a bent pin with a guarded point, used to fasten cloth.

clue.text: Count on pub profit

definitions.note: the answer is used in the phrase 'bargain on', meaning to expect

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A publican relies on the bar making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count on' looks like wordplay but is the definition, in the sense of 'bargain on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain on something is to expect or rely on it happening, as to count on it does.

clue.text: Reliable social worker missing in Santa Fe

indicators.note: the worker is absent from the city name, so its letters are removed

parts.note: the capital of New Mexico
an ant is a worker among social insects

explanation.surface: A dependable welfare officer has gone missing in a New Mexico city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare officer, but the setter means the ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe means secure and dependable, a straightforward synonym for reliable.

clue.text: Round the German river

parts.note: O is round in shape
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A German river is described as winding around.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a central European river forming much of the border between Germany and Poland.

clue.text: Send terms of reference

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to transmit money as payment
second meaning: the scope of a person's task or authority

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense is pronounced with stress on the second syllable, the noun sense on the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to dispatch payment; a remit is the defined area of responsibility given to a committee.

clue.text: Withdrew, injured

definitions.meaning: first meaning: took a horse or competitor out of a race
second meaning: grazed or wounded slightly by claws or thorns

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like an athlete pulling out hurt; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner scratched from a race has been withdrawn, and skin that is scratched has been slightly hurt.

clue.text: On intimate terms in passing romance

parts.note: handing something over is passing it
love is romance

explanation.surface: A couple drift into closeness through a brief love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like it means fleeting, describing the romance; it is the verb for handing over.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand in glove is an idiom for being in close, often conspiratorial, association with someone.

clue.text: I'm one to make writer's point

definitions.text: I'm one to make writer's point

parts.words: I'm one to make writer's point
parts.note: surface reading: someone who helps an author get an argument across
setter's reading: the writer is a pencil and its point is the sharp tip

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like an editor speaking; the 'writer' is a pencil and the 'point' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: This small bladed device shaves wood and graphite to put a fresh tip on a pencil.

clue.text: Certain phrases may be meaningless, mother admitted

indicators.note: being admitted means let inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: idiotic means senseless
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Some expressions seem nonsensical, as a mother concedes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole opening phrase: an idiom's meaning cannot be worked out from its words, which is why such phrases may seem meaningless.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic expressions are fixed phrases whose sense differs from their literal words, so certain phrases may be described that way.

clue.text: Still lacking rank?

parts.note: not with means without
standing is status or rank

explanation.surface: Someone remains without social status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb of time, 'yet', but is the sense 'nevertheless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding as an adverb means nevertheless or all the same, the concessive sense of still.

clue.text: Tots toss up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to spin a coin is to toss it

explanation.surface: Small children throw something into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tots' suggests toddlers; here they are small measures of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a small drink of spirits, the same as a tot of whisky.

clue.text: Male in possession of gold and silver crossing centre of Delhi to get transport

indicators.note: possessing something means holding it, so the male encloses what follows
the two metals cross over the middle letter, so it sits between them inside the enclosure

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter, the one kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the Indian city's name
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A man carrying precious metals across India's capital needs a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' joins the metals with Delhi's middle letter between them, and the male pronoun holds the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Haulage is the commercial carrying of goods by road, a kind of transport.

clue.text: Ate nuts, nuts causing an illness

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the preceding letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eats nuts and falls sick as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'nuts' is the anagram signal, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is a bacterial infection causing muscle spasms and lockjaw, so it is a disease.

clue.text: Vessel taking quantity of fuel round the east

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a gallon is a measure of fuel
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A ship loads fuel for its voyage around the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, a type of vessel.

clue.text: Most important soldier on scale

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
to scale a wall is to mount it

explanation.surface: The key thing is a soldier climbing a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' reads as a noun for size or measuring; it is the verb to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme or of chief importance, a synonym for most important.

clue.text: A new member returned with a backer

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the limb word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member

explanation.surface: A fresh member rejoins a club alongside a financial supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' means a limb here, not a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is someone who invests money in a theatrical production, a financial supporter.

clue.text: A young lady, out of order

parts.note: taken as written
miss is the title for a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl is behaving improperly.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means wrong or faulty, so something amiss is not working properly.

clue.text: Energy worker back on high peak

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

indicators.note: going back means travelling in reverse, so the worker's letters are read right to left

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A tireless labourer returns to a mountain summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the tall active volcano on Sicily, the highest mountain in Italy south of the Alps.

clue.text: Odious negative is first to overwhelm me

parts.note: no is a negative reply
taken as written

indicators.note: first to signals the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of overwhelm
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a hateful refusal is the first thing to swamp them.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of smells, so it is a synonym for odious.

clue.text: Admission made by expert striding around ship

indicators.note: striding over something means straddling it, so the expert word sits either side

parts.note: an ace is an expert
c is short for circa, Latin for around
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Entry is gained by a skilled person walking round a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like part of the container instruction but is a piece itself, circa abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Access is the right or means of entering a place, the same as admission.

clue.text: Irish novelist, reportedly, is demanding

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: Laurence Sterne, Irish-born author of Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: An Irish writer is said to be strict.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means severe and strict, so a stern teacher is a demanding one.
